reason: The quotas table row gives io2 storage a default of Each supported Region: 20, adjustable Yes, described as the maximum aggregated TiB across io2 volumes in this Region.
The quote states the Concurrent snapshot copies per destination Region quota is not adjustable using Service Quotas, but an increase can be requested by contacting AWS Support.
The quotas table row gives Snapshots per Region a default of Each supported Region: 100,000, adjustable Yes.
The row supports 50 TiB in 16 named Regions and 300 TiB in each other Region, adjustable; but the claim calls the 16 named Regions 'the larger Regions', a characterization the quote does not make.
The quotas table row gives StartSnapshot pending snapshots per account a value of Each supported Region: 100, adjustable No.
The quotas table row gives time-based snapshot copy throughput per destination Region a default of 2,000, in MiB/sec at account level, adjustable Yes.
The quote states EBS monitors storage and IOPS usage per Region and might automatically increase quotas per Region; the same bullet gives the example of requesting an increase ahead of planned usage.
The quote states RAID arrays larger than 8 volumes might have diminished performance returns due to increased I/O overhead.
The quotes state RAID 0 gives higher file system performance than a single EBS volume can provision, and adding a volume gives the straight addition of throughput and IOPS.
The quote states stripe performance is limited to the worst performing volume and the loss of a single volume results in complete data loss for the array.
The quote states RAID 1 is not recommended with EBS, needs more EC2-to-EBS bandwidth because data is written to multiple volumes simultaneously, and gives no write performance improvement.
The quote states RAID 5 and RAID 6 are not recommended for EBS because parity writes consume some of the IOPS available to the volumes.
The decision guide quotes recommend EBS for quickly accessible data needing long-term persistence and describe block storage as direct-attached to a compute instance with low-latency access.
Under Pricing, the quotes state no additional charges for Recycle Bin and retention rules, and snapshots and volumes in the Recycle Bin are billed at the same rate as regular ones.
The quotes state restore is possible any time before the retention period expires and an unrestored resource is then permanently deleted and no longer available for recovery.
The quote states you must create retention rules in the Regions where you want protection; the context lists resource type, rule type and retention period as what a rule specifies.
The quote states Recycle Bin restores accidentally deleted EBS volumes, snapshots and EBS-backed AMIs, retained for a period you specify before permanent deletion.
The quotes support locking, the unlock delay and unlocked-by-default, but the claim drops the condition in the same context that Region-level rules with exclusion tags cannot be locked.
Under the supported retention periods, the quote line states EBS snapshots and EBS-backed AMIs: 1 - 365 days.

The quotes and context state tag-level rules retain resources with at least one of the rule's tag pairs, and Region-level rules apply by default to all resources of the type even untagged, minus exclusion tags.
The quote states Region-level rules can optionally be locked on creation, a locked rule needs an unlock delay period of 7 to 30 days, and rules remain unlocked by default.

The first quote sits under the existing-volume option only, and the second covers volumes created by the task from a snapshot or AMI; the page's outcomes table marks encryption by default as not applicable for the existing-volume option, so 'always encrypted' overreaches.
The same sentence appears verbatim under both the launch-state and the 'Replace the root volume using a snapshot' headings of the page: same type, size and delete on termination attributes.

The quotes and the list they introduce state root replacement on a running instance keeps instance store data, non-root EBS volumes and network configuration, with an automatic reboot that erases RAM.
Under Limitations, the quote states an io1, io2, gp2, gp3 or standard root volume cannot be modified to st1 or sc1, even if detached.
Under Cold HDD volumes, the quote states a 1-TiB sc1 volume bursts to 80 MiB/s and its bucket fills with credits at 12 MiB/s.
Under Cold HDD volumes, the quote states baseline throughput varies from 1.5 MiB/s to a maximum of 192 MiB/s over 0.125 to 16 TiB, reached at 16 TiB.
Under Cold HDD volumes, the quote states burst throughput varies from 10 MiB/s to a cap of 250 MiB/s reached at 3.125 TiB.
The volume types page states sc1 provides the lowest cost per GB of all EBS volume types and is ideal for less frequently accessed workloads with large, cold datasets.
Under Cold HDD volumes, the quote states throughput is capped at a maximum of 250 MiB/s and limited to a baseline of 12 MiB/s per TiB after the bucket is depleted.
The sc1 pricing example uses a Region that charges $0.015 per GB-month, and the claim keeps it as the example Region rate.
Under the sc1 heading the use-case line reads 'Colder data requiring fewer scans per day', and the user guide calls sc1 a good fit for large, sequential cold-data workloads.
The tip recommends re-encrypting a shared encrypted snapshot by copying it with a KMS key you own, to keep access if the original key is compromised or the owner revokes access.
The quote states deleting a snapshot has no effect on the volume and deleting a volume has no effect on the snapshots made from it.
The quotes state snapshot creation is asynchronous and stays pending until data reaches S3, the volume can be used meanwhile, and the FAQ says no unmount is needed.
The quote states snapshots encrypted with the default AWS managed key cannot be shared and only those encrypted with a customer managed key can be shared.
The quote states that after block public access for snapshots is enabled in a Region, any attempt to publicly share snapshots there is automatically blocked.
The quote states a declarative policy can apply the setting across multiple Regions and accounts simultaneously, and while it is in use the setting cannot be modified directly in an account.
Under Pricing, the quote states block public access for snapshots can be enabled at no additional cost.
The quotes state block public access for snapshots does not prevent private sharing or public sharing of EBS-backed AMIs; the context says block public access for AMIs prevents the latter.
